analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and rewrites the `backend.enabled_models` row (head line 201). The new text says a background `start` and a successful `switch` save their complete nonempty selection. It also says a nonempty list, together with the models the daemon started with, acts as the running daemon's operator filter. Without Autopilot, coordinator `load_model`, `prefetch_model` and `desired_models` (including alias successors) then never load, download or advertise a model outside it. A live `switch` replaces the filter at once, and a hand edit applies at the next start. `[]` filters nothing. The row cites `ProviderLoop+ModelSelection.swift` (`operatorFilterAllows`).

Security effect, if the documentation matches the code: the provider-side filter narrows what the coordinator can make a provider load or advertise. That is a tightening relevant to TB-002 and A-018, and it does not weaken any control. No code changed in the supplied evidence, so the implementation is not verifiable here. I could not confirm that `operatorFilterAllows` enforces the stated behavior (including the Autopilot exception), that alias-successor handling cannot bypass the filter, or that the desired_models path is covered.

The remainder of the file (head lines 1-312, plus base lines 1458-1657) is unchanged context: add-on hold, sandbox CLI, endpoint resumption/logout, prefix cache and App Attest worker flags. Those sections stay consistent with TB-011, TB-012, TB-013 and T-041. No new attack surface or invalidated threat-model assumption was identified, and the patch excerpt is truncated. The enforcement code should be reviewed if it appears in another batch. I flag no finding.
